inline_comments.comment: The `useRef` declaration and accompanying `useEffect` are placed ~145 lines into the component body, after a large block of derived variable calculations. Hooks buried this deep are hard to discover during future maintenance. Consider either grouping them near the top of the component (referencing `componentTestStatusValueToStoryIds` etc. will still work since they're defined earlier) or extracting the announcement logic into a dedicated custom hook (e.g. `useTestProviderAnnouncements`).

`componentTestStatusValueToStoryIds` and `a11yStatusValueToStoryIds` are likely new object references on every render (computed inline from status arrays). Including them in the dependency array means this effect re-executes on every render, not just when `testProviderState` changes. The `prevState === testProviderState` guard prevents spurious announcements, but the effect body still runs and writes to `prevTestProviderStateRef` each time. Consider stabilising these objects with `useMemo`, or reading them from refs at the time of a state transition so they can be dropped from the dependency array.

The JSDoc says `string for **exact** match`, but the implementation on line 59 uses `content.includes(text)`, which is a **substring** match. A live region containing `"3 tests passed today"` would match `{ text: 'tests passed' }`, which may not be intended. Either change the implementation to use `content === text` for exact matching (and update the test on line 16 of the test file accordingly), or correct the doc to say `string for substring match`.

The import path `'../../../../core/src/manager/utils/toHaveLiveRegion'` crosses four directory levels into another workspace package via a raw relative path. This is brittle — any reorganisation of either package's directory structure silently breaks it. The `code/core` package is already available under the `storybook/internal/*` namespace; if this utility is intended for broader use, it should be exported from there. Alternatively, if it's test-only, a path alias configured in `tsconfig` or `vite.config` would be more resilient.

general_comments.comment: `toHaveLiveRegion` is registered via `expect.extend({ toHaveLiveRegion })` in the stories file, but there is no TypeScript declaration merging (e.g., `declare module 'vitest' { interface Matchers<R> { toHaveLiveRegion(options: LiveRegionMatcherOptions): R; } }`) anywhere in the added code. Without this, TypeScript will produce a type error at every `.toHaveLiveRegion(...)` call site and editors won't provide autocomplete. A type declaration should be co-located in `toHaveLiveRegion.ts` or added to a global types file.

The PR description states that `extend-to-be-announced` is added as a devDependency and registered in `code/.storybook/storybook.setup.ts`, and the Usage section shows a `toBeAnnounced` assertion pattern. However, none of these changes appear in the diff: `extend-to-be-announced` is absent from `package.json`, `storybook.setup.ts` is unchanged, and `toBeAnnounced` is not used anywhere in the added code. The actual stories rely solely on `toHaveLiveRegion` (DOM inspection). The description should be updated to match the actual implementation, or the intended `extend-to-be-announced` integration should be completed, since the two strategies differ meaningfully: DOM inspection can miss announcements that are cleared before the assertion runs.
